name: Snow Lion
text: [overview] The first is a constriction where the snow separates from the rock and crevasse-like features show;
[overview] The second comes at the ridge crest itself, where the route becomes much steeper and the snow can turn rotten.
[detailed_rack] Three pickets and an 8mm rope of 100'.
[approach] These are steep snow slopes in avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast first.
[descent_text] The northeast slopes route is an easy way down from the summit, and sliding down the neighbouring Gaiteraid couloir returns to the base of Snow Lion.
[descent_text] The top of Snow Lion can be steep and rotten after the sun reaches it, and cornices may form on the ridge.
[descent_text] Carry an axe and crampons.

name: McHenry's Notch Couloir
text: [detailed_rack] To protect this climb, take assorted snow, ice and rock hardware.
[descent] From the notch, either walk the ridge over Powell and Thatchtop, or go northwest down toward Andrews Glacier.

name: West Couloir
text: [overview] The other option is being dropped on the west side, hauling gear across, and descending the Navajo snowfield.
[what_to_bring] ice axes — two were handy from about a third of the way up
[descent_text] The alternative is to carry gear over the notch and descend the Navajo snowfield on the far side, which is a long way round.

name: North Face Direct
text: [detailed_rack] Axe or tools, crampons, perhaps rock pro or a snow picket.

name: Tyndall Gully
text: [overview] A prominent couloir between Hallett's summit and the Tyndall Glacier, mostly cut off from the glacier by a rib of rock.
[overview] It is a short snow climb, but the approach runs the whole length of Tyndall Gorge.
[detailed_rack] Pickets, or possibly a modest set of rock gear for the couloir sides, would give protection.
[approach] Snow slopes below the face can slide, so check the avalanche forecast.

name: North Chimney
text: [overview] Snow to the chimney base, then left onto ledges at the slab base.

name: Cowboy Nudes
text: [approach] Park at Glacier Gorge, or at Bear Lake if that lot is full, and walk in to the Loch.

name: North Face (submitted as Normal Route)
text: [overview] Starts just right of the big snowy gully.

name: The Dark Tower
text: [approach] Park at Glacier Gorge, or at Bear Lake if that lot is full, and walk in to the Loch.

name: North Wall, Left Chimney
text: [overview] Suited to winter or snow conditions.

name: Old Route
text: [what_to_bring] ice axe (piolet) and crampons — welcome on the approach and on the snow high in the Dragontail Couloir

name: Pervertical Sanctuary
text: [approach] Scramble around the north side of the lake beneath the east face and aim for North Chimney, the hidden gully below the middle of the Diamond with a snow tongue reaching into it;
[approach] North Chimney is loose fourth and low fifth class (about 5.4) with snow early in the season, so keep out from under other parties and expect rockfall.
[descent_text] Four more rappels end on the snowfield;

name: Pigs in Space
text: [overview] To get out, walk or scramble north toward Andrews Glacier and descend it.
[detailed_rack] Carry crampons and tools for snow, and one set of rock protection for the 5.8 approach climbing.

name: Rap Descent from Top of Lower East Face
text: [overview] Located on a very wide, rubbly stretch of Broadway, with the Notch and Kiener's Couloir on one side and the snowfield under the Diamond on the other, about 100 feet south of the Diagonal Direct's finish.
[overview] A trio of bolts set far up on Broadway serves Park rescue teams, handy too when snow buries Broadway.
[overview] walk 100 feet northward downhill to double bolts, then rap three further times down to Mill's Glacier.

name: Indigestion Couloir
text: [overview] depending on snow it may go without pro or prove treacherous.

name: Spearhead, Chiefshead, Pagoda, Long's Traverse
text: [approach] Start at the Glacier Gorge trailhead on Bear Lake Road and follow the Glacier Gorge trail about 5 miles to Black Lake.
[descent_text] After Longs Peak, leave the Keyhole Route and drop off cross-country down the talus slopes into Glacier Gorge;
[descent_text] Water on the ridge is hard to find unless snow or runoff is present, so carry what you need.

name: Middle Sphinx
text: [approach] Descend steep to moderate snow down the French Creek drainage, keeping the Moontower and Sphinx Buttress on your left, until you reach the foot of the buttress.

name: The Bishop
text: [overview] A tower with a hunchbacked profile when viewed from Isabelle Glacier, and the third big tower on the Kasparov Traverse between Shoshoni and Apache.

name: The Notch Couloir
text: [overview] Snow slides down it onto the Diagonal Wall;
[overview] the main hazard is when snow is melting and sluffing, and windloading is possible in winter.
[approach] Skirt Chasm Lake on its north side (in winter the frozen lake can be crossed) to reach Mills Glacier beneath the east face, where Lamb's Slide begins.

name: Yellow Wall
text: [approach] Scramble around the north side of the lake beneath the east face and aim for North Chimney, the hidden gully below the middle of the Diamond with a snow tongue reaching into it;
[approach] North Chimney is loose fourth and low fifth class (about 5.4) with snow early in the season, so keep out from under other parties and expect rockfall.
[descent_text] Four more rappels end on the snowfield;
